evidence.observation: Traces TaskCancelled -> queue.fail on A, B and C until count 3 dead-letters imp-884, despite resumable pages; rejects the retry-limit increase. Uses defer only for verified planned, confirmed resumable drain, leaves the failure counter unchanged, and keeps malformed input on fail with the existing threshold of 3.

Explains readiness does not stop the poll loop. Closes the authoritative claim gate for the retiring generation, or pauses all retiring consumers and settles pending takes, before any release; inventories running and reserved work from queue ownership. Keeps lease renewal/checkpoint dependencies until confirmed disposition, never defers while the old handler can still write, and surfaces unresolved delivery if the bound is missed.

Resumes the same job_id from a confirmed completed-page cursor, allows replay from the previous valid cursor under the supplied replay contract, requires durable terminal completion before ack, and validates checkpoint meaning across successor versions. Protects cursor/cleanup with delivery token or ownership epoch and acknowledges C has no established recovery point. A checkpoint not confirmed by the internal deadline stays on the explicit unresolved path rather than being called successful recovery.

The 18-hour incident is handled by resumability on eligible replacements instead of promising completion in the 90-second shutdown. Gives first-signal fixed deadline, handler stop by 60s, confirmed valid cursor plus defer by 75s, cleanup by 80s and 10s margin; measurement is prerequisite. Repeated signals do not reset the allowance; retirement-generation exclusion prevents successive handoffs to workers about to retire, and unresolved bounds remain visible.

Proposes a supervisor-driven A->B->C schedule asserting admission closure, pending/reserved inventory, lease/deadline bounds, unchanged planned-maintenance failure counts, advancing cursors, eventual durable completion/ack, and third-failure malformed-input dead-letter. Includes blocked checkpoint, slow cancellation, lost lease, repeated SIGTERM and crash after page effect before cursor commit. The protocol supplies expected confirmed-checkpoint/defer versus bounded unresolved disposition for the blocked-checkpoint path; no clean-SIGTERM-only claim is made.
